text:
Was I not once possessed of a gentle, heroic, fabulous youth, worthy of being written on golden leaves?—Too much luck! By what crime, by what error, have I deserved my present weakness? You who maintain that beasts sob with sorrow, that the sick despair, that the dead have nightmares, try to relate my torpor and my fall. For as for me, I can no longer express myself except like the beggar with his continual
Pater
and
Ave Maria
. I no longer even know how to speak!


Nevertheless, today at last, I believe I have finished the account of my hell. It was surely hell; the ancient one, the one where the son of man opened the doors.


From the same desert, in the same night, my tired eyes always awaken to the silver star, without the Kings of life being moved—the three magi, the heart, the soul, the spirit. When shall we go, beyond the shores and mountains, to greet the birth of the new work, of the new wisdom, the flight from tyrants and demons, the end of superstition, to adore—the first!—Christmas upon the earth?


The song of the heavens, the march of peoples! Slaves, let us not curse life.




A Season in Hell
, 1873

translation.title: Tomorrow
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish rendering, rather than from Rimbaud's French original. The prose paragraphs, standalone Pater/Ave Maria lines, rhetorical questions, and closing work/date attribution are preserved.
